newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Bidders line up for Guatemalan power plants.
newsitem.headline: Bidders line up for Guatemalan power plants.

text.p: Seventeen companies have entered the preliminary competition to purchase two electricity plants for $30 million as Guatemala privatizes electricity production, company officials and consultants said on Monday.
"Growing competition in the electricity sector in the U.S. is making people look elsewhere," Peter Macauley of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
In Guatemala, "the geography is right, the peace treaty is in place, you have a government espousing private sector principles and free enterprise principles," he said.
--AES Americas Inc., of AES Corp in Arlington, Virginia
--Enron Caribe IV Ltd. of Houston-based Enron Corp

Each company has paid $2,500 in the bid qualification process, which was extended to June 12. Despite the interest, not all 17 companies are likely to make final bids, Macaulay said. The winning bid is to be chosen on July 30.
The Guatemalan Electric Company (EEGSA) is selling the thermoelectric plants, with a combined capacity of 80 megawatts, under the General Electricity Law passed by Congress in September.
The winning bid will offer the best package in terms of price per kilowatt hour and capacity. The $30 million purchase price is fixed.

Sale of the Laguna plant in Amatitlan, about 12 miles (20 km) from the capital and the Stewart & Stevenson plant in the coastal province of Escuintla is designed to reduce debt and improve and expand service.

Barely 47 percent of Guatemalans have access to electrical service, according to EEGSA. Energy officials hope to serve 70 percent by 2000, and to increase capacity of the two plants to 150 megawatts within 18 years.
